描述_ZN: Scroll of "Mugun Offering Longevity", painted by Ren Xiong in the Qing Dynasty, on silk with color, 162.3 cm in length and 86.2 cm in width.　　The story of "Mugun offering longevity" is a myth and legend that has been widely circulated in China. According to legend, Magu was a simple and beautiful folk woman who became a fairy after her death and lived on Penglai Fairy Island. Every year, when the highly respected Queen Mother of the West celebrated her birthday, Ma Gu would use Lingzhi grass to make fairy wine and offer it to the Queen Mother of the West as a birthday gift, so Ma Gu was also named "female longevity fairy" by the Queen Mother of the West.　　The picture depicts a red cloak-clad majolica, which is simple, quiet and dignified, changing the image of "sickly" ladies painted by Fei Danxu and Cai Qi since the mid-Qing Dynasty, which is healthy and fresh. The coloring in this painting is flamboyant and decorative, and the lines are strong and expressive, complementing the figures painted.
